marks.gloss_en: Abaye: actually, [women's exemption from] sukkah is the halakha (answering הי קרא והי הלכתא: so the Yom Kippur inclusion is the verse's)
the sukkah verse's 'THE homeborn' is to include converts
the Yom Kippur verse's 'THE homeborn' is needed only [to include women] in the addition to the affliction
גדולים נמי קרו? -- older children also call for their mother on waking, so the sign does not mark the minor who no longer needs her
אלא אימא: כל שנעור ואינו קורא ״אמא, אמא!״ (= p_shimon_neor_ima_ima; Steinsaltz: calling repeatedly until she comes)
the school of R' Yannai: any [child] who relieves himself and his mother does not wipe him
אמר מר: ״כל״ לרבות את הקטנים. והתנן: נשים ועבדים וקטנים פטורין מן הסוכה!
לא קשיא: כאן בקטן שהגיע לחינוך, כאן בקטן שלא הגיע לחינוך (= p_kan_behigia_lechinuch)
קטן שהגיע לחינוך מדרבנן הוא! -- a rabbinic obligation is not derived from a verse
מדרבנן, וקרא אסמכתא בעלמא הוא (= p_kra_asmachta_ktanim)
the baraita's inclusion speaks of a minor who has reached the age of training; the mishnah's exemption of one who has not
מעשה לסתור? -- does the mishnah cite an incident (a sukkah for a newborn) that contradicts its own exemption of minors?
חסורי מחסרא והכי קתני: ושמאי מחמיר, ומעשה נמי... -- the maaseh does not contradict the anonymous rule; it illustrates Shammai's dissenting stringency (p_chasurei_mechasra, p_shammai_machmir)
the mishnah is lacking, and this is what it teaches
all seven days a person makes his sukkah permanent and his house temporary
איני?! והאמר רבא: מקרא ומתנא במטללתא ותנויי בר ממטללתא -- is that so? Rava said analysis is done outside the sukkah (kind svara under protest: no kind names an amoraic-memra contradiction, §12)
לא קשיא: הא במגרס, הא בעיוני -- the baraita speaks of running study, Rava of close analysis (p_ha_bemigras, p_ha_beiyunei)
Rava: Scripture and Mishnah [are studied] in the sukkah
the baraita: all seven days a person makes his sukkah permanent and his house temporary
